title: Alphabet & classical sounds
standardSummary: Show classical pronunciation knowledge: matching sounds, select-all hard consonants, and a short answer on macrons.
teach:
## Classical pronunciation (starter)

We use **classical** reconstruction (roughly the late Republic / early Empire), not ecclesiastical.

### Consonants to watch

- **c** and **g** are always hard: *Caesar* ~ "Ky-sar", *genus* with hard g.
- **v** is like English **w**: *via* ~ "wee-ah".
- **i** can be a vowel or a consonant (like y in *yes*) before another vowel: *Iūlius*.
- **s** is always unvoiced (no "z" sound between vowels).

### Vowels

Latin has long and short vowels. We mark long vowels with a **macron** (ā ē ī ō ū) in teaching charts. For typing answers in this app, **macrons are optional** unless a lesson is specifically about quantity.

Diphthongs: **ae**, **au**, **oe** (and **ei**, **eu**, **ui** in some words).

### Stress

Stress usually falls on the **second-to-last** syllable if it is long, otherwise on the **third-to-last**.

seeds.prompt: Match each letter or mark to its classical value.
Select ALL letters that stay hard (never soft) in classical pronunciation.

options.label: v (as a soft fricative like English v)

seeds.prompt: Put these stress-rule steps in the right order (first → last).

items.label: If it is long, stress it
If it is short, stress the third-to-last instead

payload.rubric: Student says the vowel is long / lengthened / long quantity. Partial if they only say "stress" without length.
